newsitem.title: GERMANY: Berlin reopens beloved symbol of consumer freedom.
newsitem.headline: Berlin reopens beloved symbol of consumer freedom.

text.p: Berliners had a chance on Tuesday to celebrate their own capitalist icon when the biggest department store in continental Europe flung open its doors after renovation.

When Berlin was still a divided city, Kaufhaus des Westens (Department Store of the West) stood as a symbol of the promised land for both the deprived citizens of the communist East and the Westerners proud to be shaking off the ravages of war.

On Tuesday thousands of Berliners crammed in to see how the 89-year-old institution they know as KaDeWe (pronounced Kah-Day-Vay) had been expanded by almost a third to give it 60,000 sq metres (72,000 sq yards) of floor space -- more than any European store outside Britain.
Like almost no other store, KaDeWe has been a touchstone of Europe's reconstruction and renewal this century.

In 1950, 180,000 people desperate to feel that they were putting the privations of World War Two and post-war reconstruction behind them came to see the store, which had been heavily bombed in the war, reopen its doors.
Later they came to cherish it as a testament to the survival of West Berlin's capitalist oasis, surrounded by the grey Berlin Wall and marooned inside communist territory.
And the Department Store of the West really did epitomise the riches of the West for many East Germans, too.

With its steel-and-glass elegance and dizzying array of fashion, gourmet delicacies and household appliances, the store was the first place many East Berliners wanted to visit when their communist system collapsed in 1989.
"It is surely not too much to say that KaDeWe is a symbol of Berlin," said Karl-Heinz Schmidt, board member of KaDeWe's parent company Karstadt, at the store's opening reception.

"We've been coming here since we were children," said Marianne Mueller, 67, visiting KaDeWe with her husband Juergen, 69. "It was always an experience and every time I'm here, I feel like Berlin has the flair of a world city again."
Reiner and Margot Schmidt, visiting the women's coats department, came from Dortmund to attend the reopening.
"We come to KaDeWe every time we are in Berlin, it's a tradition," said Margot. "You can feel the sense of nostalgia for the old Berlin when you're in this place. But it's even more beautiful today."

The new store has moved with the times, giving itself modern trappings almost unheard-of in Germany like a free day-care centre complete with beepers for shopping parents and a restaurant with a non-smoking section.
Karstadt is predicting the store's annual sales will leap 400 million marks ($270 million) to around a billion marks ($670 million in the next four years.
